description:
Digital to Wave 2 de Broglie is a SYNTHETIC matter-wave test, in Python (3.11–3.13), of the object hologram claimed in Mun Seok Lee's preprint Digital to Wave: LGD In Situ Wave Memory-Human Wave Integrated Interface-Metaverse Hologram- Wave Affective AI (Part II, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21947108). The preprint supplies the numbers; the computation, pass/fail criterion and tests are this project's own. Its author has not reviewed or endorsed this software.

What is included

  • The relativistic de Broglie wavelength, λ = h / √(2mℰ + ℰ²/c²), the paper's own formula, applied to the paper's own numbers: CMB peculiar velocity 370 km/s, LGD lattice pitch a₀ = 0.356 nm, THz band 300 GHz–3 THz.
  • The matter wavelength for electron, proton, 1 kg, 70 kg and 1000 kg masses at the CMB velocity and at thermal velocity (300 K), the ratios to the THz wavelength and to the lattice pitch, the phase across one lattice spacing, and the mass whose matter wavelength would equal the THz wavelength.
  • A pass/fail criterion (FAIL if the matter wavelength is ≥ 10 orders of magnitude below the THz wavelength for every macroscopic mass at every paper velocity and every THz frequency).
  • A pytest suite (5 tests) and a one-page report with the numbers, the verdict and the honest caveats.

Results (SYNTHETIC)

  • Verdict: FAIL. For 70 kg at 370 km/s the matter wavelength is 2.56 × 10−41 m, 1.17 × 1037 times shorter than the 1 THz wavelength, with a phase of 8.74 × 1031 rad across one lattice spacing.
  • Even the most generous macroscopic case (1 kg, thermal, 300 GHz) is short by 1.68 × 1019.
  • The mass whose matter wavelength would equal the 1 THz wavelength is 5.97 × 10−36 kg at 370 km/s (3.93 × 10−40 kg thermal) — about 105 times lighter than an electron.

Limits

No physical, biological or safety claim is made. This is a classical-physics bound applied to the paper's own numbers, not an experiment. It shows the claimed matter-wave storage mechanism cannot work as described; it does not test any other hologram mechanism the paper does not specify.
title: Digital to Wave 2 de Broglie: a matter-wave test of the object hologram claimed in Part II
